messages:
Support Bot: high-priority ticket from AcmeCorp: "Assistant answers changed after last model rollout — started ~12:10 UTC. Outputs now fabricate dates and drop policy clauses." :rotating_light:

Priya Singh: tagging eng-runtime and oncall. can someone triage? they included examples and say it started after today's 12:05 deploy.

Julian Park: I'm on it. which model + rollout id? any logs?

Samir Patel: Per telemetry, the prod model was rolled from redwood-open-1@v2.2.1 -> v2.3.0 at 2024-07-24T12:04:18Z (rollout id r-20240724-34). Canary 20% -> gradual ramp started.

Maria Chen: copying customer repro. They sent the prompt and two outputs (before/after). Example prompt: 

```
User: "Please summarize the compliance obligations for storing EU customer data and cite the regulation."

Expected (v2.2.1): "Summary: You must store EU personal data under GDPR Article 6; use lawful basis, maintain processing records, appoint DPO when applicable, implement data minimization, and follow cross-border transfer rules (Standard Contractual Clauses or SCCs). See GDPR Art. 6, Art. 30."

Observed (v2.3.0): "Summary: You can store EU customer data freely if anonymized. Transfers are allowed with company policy. See company policy."
```

Priya Singh: that "freely" bit is a big hallucination. we need repro steps. Maria, can you paste the curl they used?

Maria Chen: they used our REST API, simplified below:

```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-open-1","version":"v2.3.0","input":"Please summarize the compliance obligations for storing EU customer data and cite the regulation.","max_tokens":256,"temperature":0.0}'
```

Julian Park: ok, reproduce locally against v2.3.0 and v2.2.1. I can run locally on a dev node. expected to be deterministic with temp=0.0 — if outputs diverge it's a regression.

Ashwin Rao: quick check of eval infra: our 'compliance-promptset' failure rate jumped from 1.2% -> 14.7% at 12:06 UTC correlating with r-20240724-34. Affected examples show omission of statutory citations and incorrect permissive language.

Samir Patel: customers affected: AcmeCorp (#5432), FinTrust (#5478), and HealthNet (#5601). All enterprise seats, opened P1s.

Priya Singh: recommend rollback to v2.2.1 immediately. opinions? we should also pause the rollout.

Julian Park: agree. rollback + block canary. also collect diffs of token-level logits if possible to find root cause.

Priya Singh: @deploy-bot can you pause rollout r-20240724-34 and run rollback to v2.2.1 for prod? If we need manual approval I'll give it.

deploy-bot: Received request: pause rollout r-20240724-34 -> initiating pause. Current canary: 20%.

deploy-bot: Rollback command prepared: `redwoodctl deploy rollback --env=prod --model=redwood-open-1 --to-version=v2.2.1 --rollout-id=r-20240724-34`

Priya Singh: approved. run it now. prioritize < 10 min window. tell SRE to monitor token-level errors and 5xx.

deploy-bot: rollback started at 2024-07-24T12:24:03Z. Target: full prod revert to v2.2.1. Estimated time to finish: ~6 minutes. Will stream progress here.

incident-bot: Alert: Canary pause acked. Routing fallback: serving traffic now shifting away from v2.3.0 -> v2.2.1.

Samir Patel: running repro now against v2.2.1 and v2.3.0 in isolated env. saving both raw responses + generation tokens.

Julian Park: added quick diff harness to compare citations & legal-entity mentions. early result: v2.3.0 tends to drop 'GDPR' and replace with vague 'privacy law'. Token-level check shows changed tokenizer handling around Unicode control chars in the training corpus — potential cause for truncated context leading to missing citations.

Maria Chen: deploy-bot update: rollback completed at 2024-07-24T12:30:51Z. Prod is now serving v2.2.1.

Priya Singh: thanks. Maria please confirm customer-facing message and ask AcmeCorp to re-run same prompt now and share outputs. We'll prioritize postmortem.

Maria Chen: messaging draft for AcmeCorp: 

"Hi — we rolled back to the prior model version (v2.2.1) which should restore previous behavior. Could you re-run your example and paste the response? We’re investigating root cause and will follow up with a timeline. Apologies for the disruption."

Ashwin Rao: action items: 1) postmortem (owner: Julian), 2) run token-diff analysis and surface likely root cause (owner: Samir), 3) add regression test to compliance prompts (owner: Ashwin), 4) notify product/legal for potential customer impact (Priya).

Julian Park: I'll own postmortem and attach the raw diffs + rollout metadata. timeline: initial draft in 24h.

Samir Patel: I'll push a temporary check in CI to compare top-3 generations for the compliance promptset between canary versions before any ramp.

Priya Singh: perfect. Priya signing off on rollback. keep monitoring for any residual issues. update this thread when AcmeCorp confirms. :thumbsup:

Support Bot: AcmeCorp acknowledged rollback and will try again, ETA ~12:40 UTC.

Maria Chen: closing note: will open a follow-up thread for the postmortem and RFC for safer canary gating (generate-output-consistency checks).

Priya Singh: thanks all. good catch & fast rollback.

-- end of thread --
